name: GitHub Copilot CLI

versions_seen.where: local: installed (copilot --version), used by the probe in a scratch COPILOT_HOME (probe:versions/1.0.98/)
https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/releases (latest stable, published 2026-10-22; releases 1.0.99 to 1.0.103 have no hook items)

cocheck_relevance: CoCheck has a profile and a user-level install (~/.copilot/hooks/cocheck.json, one entry per event incl. subagentStop). Calls inside a helper carry agentId and parentAgentId, so they are credited to the helper under the main session; a failing shell command is read from the exit code in the result text. The cloud coding agent is unsupported (discrepancies.json copilot-cloud-agent-unsupported); with the sandbox on the hook needs a userPolicy grant (copilot-sandbox-hooks-need-policy).

install.claim: Homebrew cask; /opt/homebrew/bin/copilot is a symlink to /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/copilot-cli/1.0.93/copilot, a Mach-O arm64 executable.
Hooks ran with COPILOT_CLI_RESOLVED_DIST_DIR=~/Library/Caches/copilot/pkg/darwin-arm64/1.0.93 (downloaded package cache) and COPILOT_CLI_BINARY_VERSION=1.0.93.

processes_and_paths.claim: COPILOT_HOME overrides the config/state dir (help: 'defaults to $HOME/.copilot'). Probe: with it set, all state (config.json, session-state, logs, session-store.db, installed-plugins) went to the scratch dir and the real ~/.copilot non-log files were byte-identical afterwards.

~/.copilot layout: config.json (JSONC with // comments, auto-managed: firstLaunchAt, trustedFolders, flags), config.json.trusted-folders.lock, command-history-state.json, open-sessions-state.json, session-store.db(+shm,wal), installed-plugins/ + .lock, ide/<uuid>.lock, servers/, sidebar-sessions-state/<hash>.json, logs/process-<epochms>-<pid>.log, session-state/<uuid>/{events.jsonl,workspace.yaml,checkpoints/index.md,files/,research/,rewind-file-snapshots/}.
User-editable settings belong in ~/.copilot/settings.json (config.json header says so); it does not exist on this Mac. Hooks may be inlined there under 'hooks'.
Hooks see env COPILOT_CLI=1, COPILOT_HOME, COPILOT_PROJECT_DIR (= cwd), COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL if set; HOME stays the real home even with COPILOT_HOME set.

auth.claim: In the scratch-COPILOT_HOME probe the CLI authenticated with no token env var and nothing in the scratch config, so the login is not kept in COPILOT_HOME/config.json (likely the OS keychain; not checked). Env tokens COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN take precedence.

available.claim: Yes. Command hooks fired for 6 events (sessionStart, userPromptSubmitted, preToolUse, postToolUse, agentStop, sessionEnd) in a real -p turn on 1.0.93.

config.claim: JSON files {"version":1,"hooks":{event:[{type:'command',bash,powershell,command,exec+args,cwd,env,timeoutSec,matcher}]}}. Sources: policy /etc/github-copilot/policy.d/*.json; repo .github/hooks/*.json, .github/copilot/settings(.local).json, .claude/settings(.local).json; user ~/.copilot/hooks/*.json (or $COPILOT_HOME/hooks/) and ~/.copilot/settings.json; plugin hooks.json; custom-agent frontmatter. All matching entries run.
Repo .github/hooks/log.json with camelCase event keys and 'bash' commands was loaded and run (cwd trusted via COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL=true).

Entry types: command (default), http (url, headers, allowedEnvVars; preToolUse needs https), prompt (sessionStart only). Event keys may be camelCase (camel payload) or PascalCase (VS Code format, snake_case payload with hook_event_name).
disableAllHooks: true in a hooks file or repo settings.json disables hooks; policy hooks ignore it.
Both a camelCase .github/hooks file and a PascalCase .claude/settings.json hook fired once per call, so a call is recorded twice, in two payload formats; nothing de-duplicates.
config.note: The probe used two different tags, so this shows both sources run, not that identical commands would be collapsed. A CoCheck install in both places would double-record. Second source: hook-calls-cl.jsonl.

config.claim: PascalCase-registered events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, SessionEnd) switch to snake_case: hook_event_name, session_id, tool_name, tool_input, tool_result{result_type, text_result_for_llm}, stop_reason, transcript_path, ISO 8601 timestamp. PermissionRequest and userPromptTransformed do not switch.
Agent-scoped hooks (custom-agent frontmatter `hooks` map) arrived in CLI v1.0.97 (2026-10-13), CLI only.
config.note: Release notes only (read through gh api), not on the doc pages.

config.claim: Trace context (traceparent, tracestate) is passed to hooks since v1.0.81 (2026-08-27).

Hook behavior changes by release: v1.0.57 and v1.0.70 preToolUse errors and exit 2 deny; v1.0.63 postToolUse matchers honored; v1.0.67 timeouts fail open; v1.0.72 the 8-block guard and stop_hook_active; v1.0.88 hooks default their cwd to the project root; v1.0.78 and v1.0.92 sessionEnd fires once per prompt-mode turn.
Hook output is one JSON object, plus progress lines of the form {"type":"progress","message":"...","temporary":true}.

trust_or_approval.claim: Repo hooks run only for a trusted folder. COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL set to exactly 'true' trusts the cwd (loading its hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers); other truthy spellings only auto-approve tools.
Real config.json has trustedFolders (one entry from an earlier probe); trust is stored there, with config.json.trusted-folders.lock beside it.
Repo hooks from an untrusted folder are skipped silently: the first probe run produced no hook log until the scratch workspaces were added to trustedFolders in the scratch config.json.
trust_or_approval.note: Recorded in the probe README (an absence, so no payload file shows it). No warning appeared in the output.

fact.claim: Observed stdin: sessionId,timestamp(epoch ms),cwd,source='new',initialPrompt. Doc adds resume/startup sources; output additionalContext.
Observed stdin: sessionId,timestamp,cwd,prompt. Output modifiedPrompt is honored only by SDK hooks, not file hooks (doc).
fact.note: modifiedPrompt is honored only by SDK hooks, not by the CLI. Re-observed on 1.0.98 (2026-10-24, probe:versions/1.0.98/hook-calls-camel.jsonl); payload shape unchanged. Also fires inside subagents (with agentId), where it looks like an extra user prompt.

fact.claim: Observed stdin: sessionId,cwd,toolName,toolArgs{command,description}. NO tool call id (it does carry timestamp, epoch ms). Doc: output permissionDecision allow/deny/ask, permissionDecisionReason, modifiedArgs; exit 2 = deny; other non-zero exit fails closed.
fact.note: Output permissionDecision allow|deny|ask and modifiedArgs (rewrites the args); 'ask' becomes deny on cloud and autopilot. Exit 2 denies; any other non-zero exit also denies (fails closed). Re-observed on 1.0.98 (2026-10-24, probe:versions/1.0.98/hook-calls-camel.jsonl); payload shape unchanged. In PascalCase (PreToolUse) the payload switches to snake_case with Claude tool names (apply_patch -> Edit, bash -> Bash, view -> Read); Edit's tool_input is the raw apply_patch text, not a {file_path} object.

fact.claim: Observed stdin: sessionId,timestamp,cwd,toolName,toolArgs,toolResult{resultType,textResultForLlm}. No call id. The session-file copy also has toolResult.sessionLog and toolTelemetry. Doc output: modifiedResult, additionalContext.
fact.note: Output modifiedResult and additionalContext (10 KB cap); cannot undo the call. Re-observed on 1.0.98 (2026-10-24, probe:versions/1.0.98/hook-calls-camel.jsonl); payload shape unchanged.

fact.claim: Observed on a tool-level failure (view of a nonexistent path): stdin has toolName, toolArgs and error as a string ('Path does not exist'); in PascalCase the tool name arrived as Read. It does NOT fire for a failing shell command.
fact.note: A failing shell command (ls on a missing dir, exit 3) arrives as postToolUse resultType success with the exit code only in the text (<shellId: N completed with exit code 3>). Exit 2 treats stdout as additionalContext (docs).

fact.claim: Observed stdin: sessionId,timestamp,cwd,transcriptPath (path to the session events.jsonl),stopReason='end_turn',stop_hook_active. Doc: output decision block/allow + reason; after 8 consecutive blocks the turn ends anyway.
fact.note: No final-message field is documented: read the transcript. Output decision block|allow (max 8 consecutive blocks). Re-observed on 1.0.98 (2026-10-24, probe:versions/1.0.98/hook-calls-camel.jsonl); payload shape unchanged. stop_hook_active is snake_case even in the camelCase payload. Inside a subagent agentStop also fires, with the subagent's own sessionId and agentId, so subagent turns look like extra stops.

fact.claim: Observed for both the custom agent `writer` and the built-in general-purpose agent: stdin has agentId, agentType, agentName, parentAgentId, transcriptPath, cwd, sessionId, timestamp (custom agent adds agentDescription and agentDisplayName).
fact.note: subagentStart does carry agentId (parentAgentId is the main sessionId). Output additionalContext; cannot block. Contradicts the docs: the built-in general-purpose agent fires start and stop (discrepancies.json copilot-builtin-subagent-fires-start-stop).

fact.claim: Observed for the custom and the built-in agent: stdin has agentId, agentType, agentName, agentDisplayName, parentAgentId, response, stopReason, stop_hook_active, transcriptPath, sessionId (the parent's), timestamp.
fact.note: Output decision block|allow (max 8 consecutive blocks) and modifiedResponse (docs). The built-in general-purpose agent does fire subagentStop in 1.0.98.
errorContext values model_call|tool_execution|system|user_input; error is {message, name, stack}. Did not fire in the 1.0.98 probe.

fact.claim: Documented only; matcher on trigger manual/auto.
fact.note: Did not fire in the 1.0.98 probe.

events.name: userPromptTransformed
events.when: after the prompt is transformed for the model

fact.claim: Observed stdin: sessionId, timestamp, cwd, prompt, transformedPrompt; fired right after userPromptSubmitted, also inside subagents. No PascalCase alias: registered as PascalCase it stays camelCase.

fact.note: notification_type values shell_completed|shell_detached_completed|agent_completed|agent_idle|permission_prompt|elicitation_dialog (docs). Did not fire in the CLI -p probe (it did fire in VS Code 1.140.0).

fact.claim: Observed stdin: sessionId, timestamp, cwd, hookName, toolName (edit, bash), toolInput, permissionSuggestions; uses toolInput, not toolArgs. Fires once per prompted tool call, between preToolUse and postToolUse; inside a subagent it keeps the parent sessionId.
fact.note: Output behavior allow|deny (only deny propagates for sandbox-bypass requests; docs). PascalCase registration does not switch the payload to snake_case (discrepancies.json copilot-permissionrequest-no-snake-case).

missing_events.claim: No per-tool-call id in any hook stdin payload; no turn or message id.
missing_events.note: Re-confirmed on 1.0.98 (2026-10-24): no payload carries a tool call id; the only id-like fields are sessionId, agentId and parentAgentId.

missing_events.claim: Cloud agent does not fire permissionRequest or notification, treats preToolUse 'ask' as deny, runs only bash/command entries, has no GITHUB_TOKEN; its preCompact fires for the auto trigger only.
There is no hook for the model's own words; narration must come from the session file.
missing_events.note: Absence in the documented event list and in the observed hook.start types.

missing_events.claim: A failing shell command is not reported as a failure: `ls` of a missing dir and `exit 3` arrived as postToolUse resultType success, exit code only in the text (<shellId: N completed with exit code 3>); postToolUseFailure did not fire for them.
missing_events.note: Seen again in VS Code 1.140.0. See discrepancies.json copilot-shell-failure-reads-as-success.

missing_events.claim: preMcpToolCall (v1.0.51, 2026-05-19, 'for hook providers') is not in the public docs and is probably an SDK or extension API, not a config event.
missing_events.note: Release notes only; do not add to the event list.

config_paths.claim: User scope: ~/.copilot/hooks/*.json ($COPILOT_HOME/hooks/) and the inline hooks field of ~/.copilot/settings.json (config.json is no longer read for hooks). Not ~/.claude/settings.json.
Repo scope, Claude Code's files: the CLI reads the hooks field of the repo's .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json.
config_paths.note: A hook CoCheck writes for Claude Code in a repo's .claude/settings.json also runs under Copilot; see discrepancies.json (copilot-reads-claude-repo-settings).

config_paths.claim: Repo scope, Claude Code local file: the CLI reads the hooks field of the repo's .claude/settings.local.json.
Repo scope inline, local file: the CLI reads the hooks field of .github/copilot/settings.local.json.
Plugin scope: hooks.json or hooks/hooks.json in the plugin install dir; custom-agent frontmatter `hooks` (CLI only).
Managed scope: /etc/github-copilot/policy.d/*.json on macOS and Linux (root-owned, not group or world writable); policy hooks are CLI-only and ignore disableAllHooks.

surfaces.claim: Copilot CLI runs hooks (all matching entries from all layers run, none override).

The cloud coding agent runs only .github/hooks/*.json on the repo default branch, bash entries only; it has no notification or permissionRequest, treats preToolUse 'ask' as deny, runs in an ephemeral Linux sandbox with a firewall allowlist.
surfaces.note: Runs on GitHub's runner, not the Mac: a hook cannot write ~/CoCheckData; only an http hook to an allowlisted host or a committed repo file carries data out.

surfaces.claim: Policy hooks and agent-scoped hooks are CLI-only; agent-scoped hooks do not run for remote or org-hosted agents.
Other IDEs (JetBrains, Xcode and the like): nothing found.

skill_and_plugin_paths.claim: Skills (SKILL.md): project .github/skills/, .claude/skills/, .agents/skills/; personal ~/.copilot/skills/ and ~/.agents/skills/ in the CLI (the VS Code page also lists ~/.claude/skills/; the CLI page does not).

A skill is instructions, with no native run-this-command field; it can tell the agent to run a bundled script through the shell tool (subject to permission prompts and allowed-tools) or to call an MCP tool.
Plugins ship hooks.json (marketplace via enabledPlugins and extraKnownMarketplaces); custom agents at ~/.copilot/agents/*.agent.md (personal).
Custom agents at the project path .github/agents and the plugin install directory were not confirmed on an official page.

sandbox_and_network.claim: Local sandbox on macOS (Seatbelt): the home directory is read-only by default, other disk blocked, local and private network and internet outbound allowed; 1.0.101 lets sandboxed commands reach localhost TCP when local access is enabled. Settings are user-level or enterprise, not repo-overridable.
sandbox_and_network.note: 2026-10-24 probe on 1.0.98: the sandbox is OFF by default ('copilot help sandbox', debug log shows "sandbox":false); it applies only with --sandbox or /sandbox enable. The Seatbelt limits described here apply only when it is on.

sandbox_and_network.claim: Hooks run inside the session sandbox when it is on: with --sandbox and no policy every hook failed (/bin/bash: <script>: Operation not permitted, exit 126), fail-open, with each failure printed into the -p output; the turn still completed.
sandbox_and_network.note: Docs agree (repo, user and plugin command hooks run inside the sandbox; policy hooks on the host; hook cwd and env do not widen access) https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-configuration.

sandbox_and_network.claim: http hooks need https; http://localhost, 127.* and [::1] are allowed only with COPILOT_HOOK_ALLOW_LOCALHOST=1, and preToolUse and permissionRequest http hooks must be https. In the cloud agent the host must be on the firewall allowlist.
Timeout (default 30 s, timeoutSec or timeout) kills the hook and is always fail-open; a non-zero exit other than 2 fails open except preToolUse, which fails closed; output cap 10 MiB.

sandbox.userPolicy in settings.json grants the hook access: with {"sandbox":{"userPolicy":{"filesystem":{"readwritePaths":[<scratch>]}}}} the hook script ran and logged, a write under HOME still failed, and 127.0.0.1 returned 200.
sandbox_and_network.note: Sandboxed run is line 32 onward of hook-calls-camel.jsonl (outside_write fail, curl 200). For CoCheck, both the hook script and ~/CoCheckData would need readwritePaths, and the grant must live in the user's settings.json.

sandbox_and_network.claim: With the sandbox off (default) a hook wrote a file under HOME outside the workspace and reached 127.0.0.1 (HTTP 200) on every event of the main run.
sandbox_and_network.note: Sandbox-off state from the debug logs (see README.md).

other_observation_channels.claim: Per-session events.jsonl: append-only JSONL, one object per line {type,id,parentId,timestamp,data}. Types seen: session.start, session.model_change, session.info, session.auto_mode_resolved, user.message, system.message, hook.start, hook.end, assistant.turn_start/turn_end, assistant.message, tool.execution_start, tool.execution_complete, permission.requested/completed, model.* (turn_started, model_call_*, message, response, messages_snapshot), session.usage_checkpoint, session.permissions_changed, session.shutdown.
hook.start/hook.end events in events.jsonl record every hook input (with hookInvocationId) and a success flag; the preToolUse input there includes toolCalls[{id,name,args}].

--output-format json emits JSONL on stdout in -p mode; --share writes a markdown transcript; --usage-output-file writes final usage JSON; OpenTelemetry via COPILOT_OTEL_ENABLED or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT; --acp runs an Agent Client Protocol server.
~/.copilot/session-store.db (SQLite) exists and indexes sessions; contents not inspected.

call_ids.claim: Session file: assistant.message.toolRequests[].toolCallId (form call_<24 alnum>) equals tool.execution_start.toolCallId, tool.execution_complete.toolCallId and permission.requested.permissionRequest.toolCallId.

Hook stdin payloads from command hooks contain NO tool call id. Join to the session file by sessionId, then match toolName+toolArgs in order (n-th preToolUse equals n-th tool.execution_start), or read the hook.start copy in events.jsonl, which carries toolCalls[].id.
sessionId in every hook payload equals the session-state folder name and session.start sessionId; agentStop gives transcriptPath to the events file.

narration_sources.name: assistant.message content (phase=commentary)
narration_sources.path: session-state/<sessionId>/events.jsonl: type=assistant.message with data.phase='commentary' and data.toolRequests non-empty; text in data.content

fact.claim: Asked to narrate, the model wrote one sentence in assistant.message.content before each tool; the event (with toolRequests) was stamped 1-5 ms before (call 1: 4-5 ms, call 2: 1-2 ms) tool.execution_start and the preToolUse hook.start. Final reply has phase=final_answer. Whether it is flushed to disk before the preToolUse command runs was not tested.
fact.note: An earlier session on this Mac had an empty content string on a tool-calling message, so narration is not guaranteed without being asked.

fact.claim: Each tool request carries a short model-written intent summary ('Count data.csv lines') even when content is empty; for bash it matches arguments.description.
A reasoning summary appeared on one of the two tool-calling messages and not the other; model-dependent. Encrypted blobs alongside are opaque.

session_files.claim: ~/.copilot/session-state/<uuid>/events.jsonl is the transcript; workspace.yaml holds id,cwd,git_root,branch,client_name,name,user_named,summary_count,fork_count,created_at,updated_at,remote_steerable,mc_* ids. One folder per session; uuid equals sessionId.
-p run prints 'copilot --resume=<sessionId>' at the end; --session-id sets the UUID for a new session, so a wrapper can choose the id.

helpers_or_subagents.claim: Subagents fire subagentStart and subagentStop (custom `writer` and the built-in general-purpose agent, both via the task tool). Every hook fired inside a subagent carries agentId, agentType and parentAgentId (the main sessionId): preToolUse, postToolUse, userPromptSubmitted, userPromptTransformed, agentStop. The subagent's own sessionId equals its agentId, except permissionRequest, which keeps the parent sessionId.
helpers_or_subagents.note: Attribution rule for CoCheck: join on agentId/parentAgentId; the inner sessionId is a new id. subagentStart carries agentId and parentAgentId directly.

helpers_or_subagents.claim: --fleet runs parallel subagent orchestration (help text). Not exercised.

limits_and_timeouts.claim: timeoutSec default 30 (alias timeout). Timeout is fail-open for every event. Non-zero exit other than 2 fails open except preToolUse, which fails closed. Output capped at 10 MiB; postToolUse extra context capped 10 KB; matcher is regex wrapped ^(?:...)$ and an invalid regex skips the entry.
Each hook command took about 3-7 ms (hook.start to hook.end) in the probe.

update_channel.claim: Auto-update downloads newer packages into ~/Library/Caches/copilot/pkg/darwin-arm64/<ver>; disable with --no-auto-update or COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false. Latest published releases seen: 1.0.98 and 1.0.100-1; the only hook-related note on that page: 'Command hooks complete reliably even when child-exit signals are lost under Node'.

open_questions: Is assistant.message flushed to events.jsonl before the preToolUse command runs? This decides whether narration is readable pre or only post. Needs a preToolUse hook that reads the transcript.
Is userPromptSubmitted before sessionStart stable in interactive mode and on resume?
Release notes for 1.0.0 to 1.0.97 hook changes were not read (only the first releases page).
Why does the session-file preToolUse input have toolCalls[].id while the stdin has toolName/toolArgs only? Could a later version add the id?
Copilot CLI: naming of MCP tools in toolName, and the events.jsonl schema beyond what the 1.0.93 recording shows.
errorOccurred, preCompact and notification did not fire in the 1.0.98 -p probe; agentStop blocking, --fleet and http hooks were not exercised.
Releases 1.0.99 to 1.0.103 have no hook items on the release page; Aug-Sep 2026 notes were skimmed through the release list only.
Scratch COPILOT_HOME kept keychain auth in the probe; does login always survive a scratch home?
